full_judgment:
ix. Failure on the part of plaintiff to bring all partible i.e. ejmali or joint properties in hotchpot. 

 II. Suit suffered from defect of hotchpotch and the suit is barred by defect of hotchpotch. 

 IV. Plaintiffs did not mention all lands noted in kabuliyat and deeds in schedule and plaintiff suit is barred by doctrine of hotchpot. In coming to said decision learned Trial Judge examined Kabuliyat and documents. 

 II. Suit is bad for defect of parties and defects of hotchpotch and hotchpot and these defects are "formal defects" and plaintiffs-petitioners may be granted permission to withdraw suit with permission to sue afresh. 

 V. Defect of parties and defect of hotchpotch are not "formal defects" going to the root of case of plaintiffs-petitioners. Md Badruddin Moral vs Santosh Kumar Sen 41 DLR (AD) 156 has been relied upon in support of contention so surged forward. 

 31. Learned Trial Judge in dismissing the suit considered evidence of PW 5 Advocate Commissioner who laid bare evidence that he on local investigation did not find the similarity with all the plots noted in kabuliyat and he, also, did not make any report. Advocate Commissioner PW 5, also, did not state the quantity of land transferred in the kabuliyat dated 21-2-1919. Learned Trial Judge found inconsistency and infirmity in respect of quantity of land converted by kabuliyat. Learned Trial Judge, also, took into account evidence of PW 5 Advocate Commissioner who laid bare in evidence that he was not at all aware of land converted in the kabuliyat. Learned Trial Judge taking into account the evidence of PW 5 Advocate Commissioner came to hold that land of Lakshmipur and Singua Mouza had been measured and there had been no identity of land conveyed in kabuliyat with the schedule land described in plaint and suit is barred by the defect of hotchpotch. Learned Appellate Judge concurred with findings reached by learned Trial Judge. 

 35. In a suit for partition all joint properties are to be brought on hotchpot i.e. all joint properties must be subject matter of partition. But plaintiff-petitioners did not make all joint properties subject matter of partition i.e. into hotchpot and learned Trial Judge, also, took into account this vital aspect. Failure on the part of plaintiffs-petitioners to bring all joint properties in the suit for partition brought about the collapse of suit and non-bringing of all joint/ejmali lands is a serious "formal defect." 

 37. In the case in hand "formal defect" on defect of parties was not the sole ground taken for withdrawal of suit with permission to sue afresh. Basic ground pressed into service for withdrawal of suit is defect of hotchpotch and hotchpot. In Messrs Ilamuddin and Sons vs Asghar Ali 1970 SCMR 233 objection raised in written statement was taken as to defect of party and it was categorically stated that Mian Hamuddin representing the petitioner's firm was a necessary party to the suit. It was further alleged that a mere declaratory suit was not maintainable and that the prayer made in the suit was vague and indefinite. Their Lordship of Pakistan Supreme Court held that all pleas of written statement obviously refers to defects in the frame of the suit. Pakistan Supreme Court overruled the objection raised by defendant that necessary party was not impleaded. Permission granted to plaintiff by Trial Court to withdraw the suit with liberty to bring fresh suit on the cause of action was maintained by the High Court of West Pakistan, Lahore in Revision and against these Judgments High Court Petition for Special Leave to Appeal before the Supreme Court of Pakistan was dismissed and permission to withdraw the suit with liberty to institute fresh suit was maintained.
